Agent.text:
I built **MatCraft**, your own design-and-cut app for Linux (Bazzite) that also runs on Windows. It builds, its self-tests pass and it opens correctly, but **it can't cut yet**: it hasn't been tested with your real machine, and the step that sends the actual cutting lines to the Maker hasn't been worked out.

**What works:**
- **Designing:** you can design on a 12 × 12 inch cutting area with shapes, text that turns into cut outlines, and SVG uploads. Pieces can be moved, resized, rotated and flipped, with layers and undo.
- **"Make it" screen:** this sorts your pieces onto one mat per colour. You pick a material and a 12 × 12 or 12 × 24 inch mat, and can save each mat as an SVG file.
- **Machine panel:** it is preset to your machine's Bluetooth address, 00:06:66:8D:2B:FE, and shows the pairing steps for Bazzite.

**What I learned from the original:** I read its program that talks to the machine. I found how its messages are packaged and encrypted, about 15 command numbers (clear errors, home the blade, stop cutting, read the buttons and lights, and so on), and the start of its "begin an encrypted session" request. The panel can send those commands and show the machine's replies.

**What it can't do yet:**
- **Cut your designs:** when you press Go, it only wakes the machine, clears errors and homes the blade. It doesn't send your cutting lines.
- **Set up encryption on its own:** that step picks from secret keys built into the original program, and I chose not to copy them. If your machine insists on encryption, you'd need to paste in a key.
- **Material settings:** the pressure and pass numbers are my estimates, because the original downloads its real settings from its online service.

All of this is written up in the app's notes sheet (its folder has the full list).

A good next step: try connecting from Bazzite with the Machine panel and tell me what the replies say. That's the quickest way to confirm the connection works before I dig into how cutting lines are sent.

Agent.text:
Yes. The Compare window now has a "Machine behaviour" tab that sets every value on the notes sheet next to what MatCraft actually does and what the original's machine program holds; you can also run the same check without opening the app.
- **How it measures MatCraft:** it runs MatCraft's own machine code: message framing, encryption, the reply reader, command contents and mat layout.

**What still isn't compared:** anything that only shows up when the original is actually talking to a machine, such as timing and the encryption handshake reply.

The app builds and all 19 self-tests pass, including one that runs this comparison. The automatic check still reports behaviour as "not compared" because it doesn't read MatCraft's own report yet; that isn't something I can fix from the app side.
